So after doing my thing with Jack Farley and stewing a bit here's some thoughts about dc's 

Let's presume that the narrative is correct and a marked slowdown in data center build has occured.  One could say it had occured anyway and without the political catalyst we had reached peak growth but let's stick with the idea that the result of the election is stalled data center build out.  

Literally all suppliers of goods and services for BUILDING new are fucked. No way around that outcome.

Let's strawman three formations of data center companies

1. Fully built already AND not planning and never priced to plan to build more (not sure if any exist). They have compute which may become scarce and prices bid up
2. Pure new build company with projects in the hopper but none built so far.  Not sure if any exist but they are fucked. Their stocks are 100% on the come.  They may have debt or committments which depend on revenues from compute that won't get built.
3. Combination of both. With obviously the mix mattering a lot. Some benefit of compute scarcity offset by future build revenue dropping and/or delayed. 

So let's deal with existing compute.  Clearly it will be scarce and prices could be bid up. IFF The buyer of compute can pay for it and or pass it on to the end buyer.    The buyer of compute is largely the frontier models as the marginal pricer.  I see that buyer burning compute to train their models with no revenue and some revenue from model sales to end users but probably very very little pricing power particularly given the slower model improvement in a scarce and expensive compute environment.  
That dynamic will increase cash burn and financing needs of frontiers. 

I can't see how the compute scarcity is net good for overall cohort profits with picks and shovels directly impacted negatively. With existing compute having some upside.  With future compute companies viability threatened. With frontiers in trouble unless they can raise prices and sell expensive tokens and slow model development 

At the same time a stall will reduce issuance volume for compute build which has been huge.

Equity risk premiums could contract while earnings expectations has to go down a lot for the whole cohort except for those narrow companies with built capacity and no other negatives.

Of course the frontier models pricing power may be poor due to Chinese models as well.

The Death of KOL-as-a-VC is a fun one:

Just until recently KOLs were actively investing in private/seed sales at better terms than top VCs.

I used to get tons of invitations to join sales at lower valuations & shorter lockups.

That all dried out.

And KOLs who actively invested in seed are mostly rekt.

But I think believe projects should try to onboard ambassador/believer KOLs to help them grow.

But choose quality over quantity. One to three flag bearer KOLs will do you good.

On the flip side, an extractor KOL will damage reputation for good.

$COHR earnings transcript TLDR:

Q: On $LITE + $MRVL merger.

A. Customers will prefer an independent optical supplier without competitive conflicts (opportunity for other merchant laser suppliers)

Q: Loop Capital asked about 2028 laser industry oversupply.

A: No oversupply risk by 2028. Coherent’s entire current internal InP production is consumed by its own products while its expanding capacity.

Q: On Chinese laser competition for CPO UHP lasers

A: “We really only have one competitor” (hinting at $LITE). 

Q: On financing concerns for capacity expansion during this market scare

A: Customer LTAs have prepayments, which are used for product capacity orders

2027 completely sold out, LTAs extend to 2030, customers placing orders into 2028.

Q: On laser technology for CPO scale up from Bernstein, whether it’s VCSELs or CW lasers.

A: CW for CPO scale out and scale up for 2026-2027.

2029-2030 sees scale in and chip to chip using micro-VCSELs, and 2028 opportunities for NPO scale up.

So technology of choice is CW for CPO.

- Coherent is seeing pricing power and raising margin targets, supporting view optical players get additional leverage for margin expansion

- Massive new $20B 5Y LTA, anchored by UHP CW lasers, with other optical products mixed in

- demand comes from growth in DC and conversion of copper interconnects to optics. The latter is bandwidth requirements, independent of DC growth.

slower compute growth can coexist with sharply rising optical content per system

TLDR:

- nothing quite showing optical demand like $20B in LTAs anchored by high power lasers from 1 customer alone (not your frontier labs type commitments)

- no industry wide laser oversupply risk by 2028 for InP lasers/EML 

- financing funded by revenue from LTAs and purchase orders.

- doesn’t see Chinese competition for high end lasers, commentary casts doubts over China capability + capacity expansion claims

- CW lasers weapon of choice for CPO, blended margins going up for optical players

- optics more isolated in the event of a DC slowdown 

Quite wild to see fundamentals of optical players improve so much, while overall valuations crash.

hard to articulate what i'm thinking here after Tuesday, but i'll give it a shot because i think it's important to understand the seismic shift occurring within both political parties in the US:

Democrats fucked themselves up in the lead up to 2024 because they over-rotated on stupid social issues as a way to stand against Trump. they thought this was legitimately their best strategy and it became their entire brand to a lot of people

ofc, it was a disaster. most people don't mind what others do in their own homes, but they don't want things forced down their throats

but what's interesting about the big wins on Tuesday is the Democrats didn't win (or even run) on these issues. though their opponents on the right tried to saddle them with that baggage, it simply didn't work

the messages which broke through were around 1) affordability, 2) ending the Iran war (which has also harmed affordability), 3) addressing somewhat vague concerns around AI-related job loss (most tangibly observed in unmitigated data center build out), and 4) stemming the substantial observable corruption within the Trump administration

social issues were almost completely absent from the Democratic platform. further, the winning platform also didn't really originate meaningfully from the traditional DNC elites. it bubbled up through a lot of younger upstart candidates, many of whom could seriously be credible as candidates for POTUS in 2028

so it's likely the Democratic talent vacuum has ended, and the Republican talent vacuum is now beginning

as a result, it's quite possible that Democrats WON'T have to go further left on social issues to recruit the votes needed to win POTUS in 2028. IF they can hold on this, then it also simultaneously makes their platform more attractive to relatively centrist Republicans who are also fed up with all of the aforementioned issues

so if Dems don't fuck up on social issues and on immigration (i.e., they need to have a credibly strong immigration policy), then they don't need the extreme left to win anymore

in isolation, this seems like it would break the two party system, but the response will be that the Republican Party moves further to the left on some issues. nativist and race-driven platforms won't work because they are inherently exclusionary. most normal people not on this site in 2026 are also not driven by racial factors in their voting decisions

so, tl;dr- big shifts are coming to both parties. Democrats will actually move more centrist on social issues while becoming more meaningfully progressive on economic issues. Republicans tbd, but they also probably move more towards the center back to economic issues the working class cares about (not just social issues)

like it or not, the race for 2028 starts now 🇺🇸
